content:
Large numbers open the Class 5 Maths Olympiad — Indian and international place value, rounding, Roman numerals and heavy-duty arithmetic all show up in IMO and SOF papers. This guide covers what the chapter tests, the facts to drill, the slips, and a free 10-question online test from our verified bank.

What the Class 5 Maths Olympiad Large Numbers and Operations chapter tests

  • Indian (lakh/crore) and international (million) place value
  • Expanded form, comparing and rounding large numbers
  • Roman numerals up to M
  • The four operations and order of operations

Key facts your child should know

  • 1 lakh = 100 thousand; 1 crore = 10 million.
  • Round by the next digit — 5 or more rounds up.
  • XL = 40, XC = 90, CM = 900 (smaller before bigger subtracts).
  • Work brackets, then × ÷, then + − : 8 + 4 × 5 = 28.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Mixing lakh-crore commas with million commas.
  • Adding before multiplying in mixed expressions.
  • Forgetting the remainder rule: remainder < divisor.

questions.q: In the number 5,27,43,618, what is the place value of the digit 7?
questions.explanation: Counting from the right, the digit 7 stands in the place worth 1,00,000, so its place value is 7 x 1,00,000 = 7,00,000.

questions.q: A box holds 6,275 pens. How many pens are there in 48 such boxes?
A farmer packs 2,744 mangoes equally into 56 boxes. How many mangoes go into each box?
questions.explanation: 2,744 divided by 56 gives 49 exactly, because 49 x 56 = 2,744.

questions.q: What must be added to 36,45,278 to get 50,00,000?
questions.explanation: Required number = 50,00,000 - 36,45,278 = 13,54,722; the subtraction borrows across the zeros of 50,00,000.
6,00,00,000 - 10,000 = 5,99,90,000; watch how the digits roll over across the zeros and nines.

questions.q: Riya's classroom clock shows chapter 64 in Roman numerals. Which is it?
questions.explanation: Break 64 into tens and ones and convert each part: 64 = LXIV.

questions.q: 94,192 bricks reach a site in 7 equal lorry-loads. How many bricks are in each load?
The numeral for "seven crore eight lakh fifty thousand three hundred forty-nine" is:
questions.explanation: Placing crores, lakhs, thousands, hundreds, tens and ones in their periods gives 7,08,50,349.
Line up the digits by place and add with carrying: 47,36,258 + 28,94,767 = 76,31,025.

faq.q: What is the difference between lakh and million?
faq.a: One lakh is 100,000 (1,00,000 in Indian commas); one million is 1,000,000 — so 10 lakh = 1 million.
The order of operations: Brackets, then Of/Orders, then Division-Multiplication left to right, then Addition-Subtraction.
